doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Boyhood band with Skeeter and a homemade kazoo
summary: Martin recalls Skeeter on bass and guitar and a boys' band in which Martin, given long pants and put in charge, played a kazoo made from a fishing pole.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Yeah. Now you take, you take, Skeeter, he played bass, eh?

Yeah, he used to play bass. He played for you. Yeah, he used to play guitar with me too. We didn't carry him long, you know. Yeah. He used to play guitar and bass. Yeah. And that's the time you all carried him in the country, eh? Oh yeah. They carried me. They carried me. They carried me. They made the whole grinding and displayed from place to place. And the name was on the book, the grinding was wrong with the fellas, the fellas dropped much money as the fellas was working at the field.

They gave me long pants to come. Yeah, I was in charge. They gave me long, long pants. Skeeter, Jackson, and Sola. Yeah. Yeah. They got a... Zuku, eh? One of them fishing poles. Henry poles. Henry poles. Henry poles. Henry poles. And I took it and bored me, cut me two holes in there and that brown smoking paper. Yeah.
Sounded like a kazoo or... Zuku, that's what it was.
That's what it was. That was our band.
The Zuku. That was our band. The Zuku.
It was ninety-six dollars and then you went in the field that day.
